root_causes.description: The frontend container was terminated ('Killing: Stopping container frontend') and replaced by a freshly scheduled pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8, causing a collapse of the frontend server request rate (p50 dropped to ~8 from a mean of ~148 req/s). Downstream services such as checkout remained normal with no elevated errors, so the disruption originates at the frontend pod itself, consistent with a container crash/restart.

evidence.observed_value: mean=148.190, p50=8.009, p95=432.873, p99=570.433, max=604.823 req/s; request-rate collapse (p50 far below mean)
evidence.expected_baseline: steady frontend server request rate ~148 req/s mean
checkout request rate unchanged; confirms fault is local to frontend, not downstream
no container termination events in steady state

evidence.query_or_id: Scheduled: Successfully assigned otel-demo/frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 to otel-sre-copilot-control-plane
evidence.observed_value: count=1; new frontend pod created (Created/Started) replacing the terminated container
evidence.expected_baseline: no new pod scheduling events in steady state

remediation_steps: Confirm frontend pod restart/crash: kubectl -n otel-demo get pods -l app=frontend and kubectl describe pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 (inspect Last State, Reason, Exit Code).
Inspect the terminated frontend container's previous logs (kubectl logs <prior-frontend-pod> --previous) to distinguish OOMKill, liveness-probe kill, or application crash.
Verify downstream services (checkout, cart, payment) recovered and that load-generator traffic to frontend is restored to ~148 req/s.
Review frontend resource requests/limits and liveness/readiness probe thresholds; add a preStop/graceful-shutdown and increase restart resilience if the crash recurs.
